title: Tide
short: Water. Strong against Ember.
lines: Hits Ember bosses for 50% more damage.
Hits Spark bosses for 25% less damage.
Tide hits leave Soaked on the boss. Spark cashes it in.

title: Ember
short: Fire. Strong against Grove.
lines: Hits Grove bosses for 50% more damage.
Hits Tide bosses for 25% less damage.
Ember hits leave Scorched on the boss. Tide cashes it in.

title: Grove
short: Plants. Strong against Spark.
lines: Hits Spark bosses for 50% more damage.
Hits Ember bosses for 25% less damage.
Grove hits leave Overgrown on the boss. Ember cashes it in.

title: Spark
short: Lightning. Strong against Tide.
lines: Hits Tide bosses for 50% more damage.
Hits Grove bosses for 25% less damage.
Spark hits leave Charged on the boss. Grove cashes it in.

title: Setter
short: Marks the boss for a combo.
lines: Its hit leaves its element's mark on the boss.
It can swap a mark of another element.
Other roles only mark a boss that has no mark.
Act before the creature that cashes the mark in.

title: Payoff
short: Hits reactions harder.
lines: A Payoff hits even harder when it sets off a reaction.
Any role can set off a reaction. Payoffs do it best.
Put it after a Setter that leaves the right mark.

title: Guard
short: Tough. Takes the hits aimed at its row.
lines: Armor: takes 25% less damage from every hit.
A hit aimed at one creature goes to a Guard in its row instead (dungeon: right beside it). Two Guards roll.
Creatures right beside it, in its row, take 40% less from hits on many creatures.
A Lance stops at a Guard. A hit aimed at a Guard never goes on to another.

title: Support
short: Powers up its neighbours.
lines: Each round it boosts the creatures right next to it. In the raid its reach stops at the row's edge.
Their next hit deals 15% more damage.
By element: Ember boosts 25%, Spark adds reaction damage, Tide and Grove heal (Tide clears silence too).
Nothing reaches past a knocked-out neighbour. A knocked-out or silenced Support gives nothing.

title: Soaked
short: Tide's mark. Spark cashes it in.
lines: Left on the boss by a Tide hit.
A Spark hit sets off Overload.
Only a Setter of another element can swap it.
It stays until it is cashed in or swapped.

title: Charged
short: Spark's mark. Grove cashes it in.
lines: Left on the boss by a Spark hit.
A Grove hit sets off Grounding.
Only a Setter of another element can swap it.
It stays until it is cashed in or swapped.

title: Overgrown
short: Grove's mark. Ember cashes it in.
lines: Left on the boss by a Grove hit.
A Ember hit sets off Wildfire.
Only a Setter of another element can swap it.
It stays until it is cashed in or swapped.

title: Scorched
short: Ember's mark. Tide cashes it in.
lines: Left on the boss by a Ember hit.
A Tide hit sets off Steam.
Only a Setter of another element can swap it.
It stays until it is cashed in or swapped.

title: Overload
short: Spark on Soaked: deals much more damage.
lines: A Spark hit on a Soaked boss sets it off.
It deals much more damage than a normal hit.
It uses up the mark. The next hit leaves a new one.
Any role can set it off. Payoffs hit even harder.

title: Grounding
short: Grove on Charged: deals much more damage.
lines: A Grove hit on a Charged boss sets it off.
It deals much more damage than a normal hit.
It uses up the mark. The next hit leaves a new one.
Any role can set it off. Payoffs hit even harder.

title: Wildfire
short: Ember on Overgrown: deals much more damage.
lines: An Ember hit on an Overgrown boss sets it off.
It deals much more damage than a normal hit.
It uses up the mark. The next hit leaves a new one.
Any role can set it off. Payoffs hit even harder.

title: Steam
short: Tide on Scorched: deals much more damage.
lines: A Tide hit on a Scorched boss sets it off.
It deals much more damage than a normal hit.
It uses up the mark. The next hit leaves a new one.
Any role can set it off. Payoffs hit even harder.

title: Zone attack
short: Hits every creature in one row. An empty row: the nearest row with someone.

title: Silence
short: The leftmost and rightmost creature still standing in each row skip a turn.

title: Reflect
short: The first reaction each round hits back at who cashed it in, or their Guard.

title: Strongest strike
short: Targets your top attacker, and may jump on.

title: Sweep
short: Hits one row, every row, or the row with the most Payoffs.

title: Barrage
short: Shells hit different random creatures. Not last volley's, if others are left.

title: Slam
short: A heavy hit, often on your best Payoff. Neighbours of the victim take a share.

title: Lance
short: Pierces one lane, front to back. A Guard stops it.

title: Pincer
short: Hits the ends of each row, or of the whole line.

title: Charge
short: Marks victims a round ahead. A fallen mark is spared. Never round 1 or overtime.

title: Front
short: Closest to the boss. Hit first.

title: Middle
short: Between Front and Back.

title: Back
short: Farthest from the boss. Hit last.

title: Left to right
short: The line acts from slot 1 on.

title: Right to left
short: The line acts from the last slot.

title: By Speed
short: Fastest creature acts first.

title: Auto fire
short: Fires abilities for you.

title: Creature ability
short: A move for the live finale.
lines: Every species has its own ability.
It unlocks at level 10 and gets stronger when the creature evolves.
Up to 3 team creatures fire one each, plus your basic ability.
Each ability fires once.

title: Basic ability
short: Everyone brings one.

title: Rally
short: Rally: everyone hits harder for a while.

title: Shield Wall
short: Shield Wall: one zone takes less damage.

title: Re-mark
short: Re-mark: puts a mark on the boss.

title: Purge
short: Purge: turns off the boss's counter-move.

title: Strike
short: Strike: hits the boss right away.

title: Boss Rank
short: How tough this week's boss is.
lines: Each Rank makes the boss stronger.
Win a normal week's finale and the Rank goes up by 1.
Lose and the Rank stays the same.
Higher Ranks pay more Essence.

title: Festival
short: Every 5th week: easier and richer.
lines: Every 5th raid week is a Festival.
The boss fights 3 Ranks lower, and Essence pays 50% more.
Win the finale to win the Festival creature.
A win keeps the Rank. After a Festival, the Rank eases by 1.

title: Season
short: 5 raid weeks, ending in a Festival.
lines: A season is 5 raid weeks.
Weeks 1 to 4 are normal. Week 5 is the Festival.
The pips show where you are. The last pip is the Festival.
Then a new season begins.

title: Readiness
short: How ready your team looks.

title: Long shot
short: Your team looks short for this boss.

title: Even
short: Could go either way.

title: Likely
short: Your team looks ready.

title: Strong
short: Your team looks very ready.

title: Counter-move
short: After Phase 1 the boss resists what worked best.

title: Retreat
short: Phase 1 or 2 floor: the boss goes immune, the fight ends, extra damage is lost.

title: Enraged
short: Out of time: your creatures act, then the boss attacks and hits every creature.

title: Essence
short: Raid reward. Evolves creatures and pays for Reach crafts.
lines: Every raid stage you clear pays Essence. Dismantling gear gives a little.
Most of it is the same for all. The rest depends on how much you helped.
Higher Ranks and Festival weeks pay more.
Evolving costs 20 Essence (40 for rare creatures). Reach crafts cost Essence too.

title: Bait
short: Currency from a daily allowance and from leets.
lines: Open the game each day for an allowance of 25 Bait. The day starts at 13:37; a missed day is not paid later.
Leeting in Discord adds a bonus of 15 to 32 Bait, more when more players leet that day.
Spend it on treats, to craft lures and to slot a talent from the Talent Book.
Trips and the other supplies cost no Bait. Releasing a duplicate pays parts, never Bait.

title: Experience
short: Creatures grow by doing things.
lines: A creature earns experience on trips, in the daily dungeon, in raid stages and on Workshop jobs.
Level 1 to 2 needs 27 experience. Level 10 to 11 needs 450. Level 20 to 21 needs 1,300.
Only creatures that take part earn it, so who goes where is your choice.

title: Treat
short: Doubles one activity's experience.
lines: Tick Pack a treat when you send a creature on a trip, put it in the dungeon team or give it a Workshop job.
That activity gives the creature double experience.
A treat costs 3 + half the creature's level (rounded up) in Bait, paid when the activity starts.
Raids take no treats.

title: Ribbon
short: A creature waits at level 10 and 20 for one.
lines: Bronze Ribbon at level 10: 6 scrap and 2 shards of its element.
Silver Ribbon at level 20: 15 scrap, 5 shards, 1 glimmer and 5 finished trips.
Experience earned while it waits is kept.
Gold Ribbon at level 30 is a reward.

title: Level
short: Higher level, stronger creature.
lines: A creature levels up from experience: trips, the dungeon, raids and Workshop jobs.
Each level adds HP, Attack and Speed.
A creature waits at level 10 and 20 for a ribbon, and at 15 until it evolves. The top is 30.
At level 10 a creature gets its finale ability.

title: Critical hit
short: A lucky hit that does extra.
lines: Every hit has a 5% chance to be critical.
A critical hit does 50% more damage.
A few creatures crit more often, or harder.
The boss can crit too, with the same odds.

title: Fusion
short: Fuse a duplicate to make a creature stronger.
lines: A duplicate catch waits as a choice. Fuse it into the creature you already have.
Each fusion adds stats, up to 20% after 5 fusions.
The stars show your fusions. After 5, Teach or Release the duplicate instead.

title: Talent
short: A small permanent bonus a creature carries.
lines: Every catch rolls one talent from its species' pool, and the card shows it first.
A creature has one slot from the start, a second at level 20 and, if rare or epic, a third at 25.
A talent works like a gear line, in raids, the dungeon and on trips.
Epic creatures also carry a fixed signature talent.

title: Golden talent
short: A rare talent, one and a half times as strong.
lines: About 1 catch in 20 rolls its talent golden, shown with a golden shimmer.
A golden talent keeps its gold in the Talent Book.

title: Talent Book
short: Every talent a creature has held.
lines: A taught talent goes into the book, and a talent a new one replaces stays in it.
Slot a talent from the book for 10 Bait, at once.

title: Duplicate
short: A catch of a creature you own is a choice.
lines: Teach: its talent goes into your creature's Talent Book. Fuse: one more fusion, up to 5.
Release: parts, never Bait.
The card marks Recommended. Up to 10 wait, then the oldest takes the Recommended choice.

title: Rarity
short: How hard a creature is to find.
lines: Common, Rare or Epic.
Rarer creatures turn up less often on expeditions.
Deeper areas, familiar places and a lucky find improve the odds.

title: Shiny
short: A rare sparkly colour.
lines: About 1 in 500 catches is shiny.
A shiny duplicate makes your creature shiny.
It is only for show. A shiny has the same stats.

title: Away
short: On an expedition.
lines: It cannot go on another trip or take a Workshop job until it is back.
Claim or recall the expedition to bring it home.

title: First on server
short: Nobody here had it before you.
lines: You were the first on this server to get it.
Everyone who got it at the same moment shares the title.

title: Gear
short: A Hat, a Scarf and a Charm for every creature.
lines: Hats and Scarves carry Attack and HP as their own stats. A Charm has a base line instead.
Every item also rolls 1 to 3 lines, each with five tiers. A creature wears items up to its own level.
Scarves open at creature level 7 and Charms at 13.
Take an item apart in the Workshop for parts and Essence. It takes a little time and cannot be undone.

title: Hat
short: The first slot. Leans to Attack and crits.
lines: Open from level 1.
Only Hats roll Crit damage and First pounce.

title: Scarf
short: Opens at creature level 7. Leans to HP and wards.
lines: Only Scarves roll All damage taken, Unbothered and Brace.

title: Charm
short: Opens at creature level 13. Roles, reactions and trips.
lines: Only Charms roll Cover, Boost, Lingering and the trip lines.
A few Charms are made for one role and can only be worn by it.

title: Item level
short: Fixed when the item drops or is crafted.
lines: It sets the best tier a line can roll: II from 5, III from 10, IV from 15, V at 20.
A creature can only wear items up to its own level.
Better Hats and Scarves unlock at item level 5 and 10. A craft needs the Crafting level for the one you pick.

title: Tier
short: How strong a line rolled: I to V.
lines: The pips show the tier rolled. The last pip is the best this item level could roll.
A tier is one fixed number. Nothing re-rolls.

title: Tag
short: An element, neutral, explorer or a role.
lines: An element tag makes that element's lines three times as likely to roll.
A role Charm can only be worn by that role.

title: Tide gear
short: Its lines lean Tide.
lines: Tide lines roll three times as often on it: Tide Attunement, Hunter and Ward, and the Tide reaction bonus.
Anyone can wear it. Tide Attunement only helps a Tide creature.
Crafting it takes a Tide shard.

title: Ember gear
short: Its lines lean Ember.
lines: Ember lines roll three times as often on it: Ember Attunement, Hunter and Ward, and the Ember reaction bonus.
Anyone can wear it. Ember Attunement only helps an Ember creature.
Crafting it takes an Ember shard.

title: Grove gear
short: Its lines lean Grove.
lines: Grove lines roll three times as often on it: Grove Attunement, Hunter and Ward, and the Grove reaction bonus.
Anyone can wear it. Grove Attunement only helps a Grove creature.
Crafting it takes a Grove shard.

title: Spark gear
short: Its lines lean Spark.
lines: Spark lines roll three times as often on it: Spark Attunement, Hunter and Ward, and the Spark reaction bonus.
Anyone can wear it. Spark Attunement only helps a Spark creature.
Crafting it takes a Spark shard.

title: Tide boss
short: Spark creatures deal it 50% more damage, Ember creatures 25% less.

title: Ember boss
short: Tide creatures deal it 50% more damage, Grove creatures 25% less.

title: Grove boss
short: Ember creatures deal it 50% more damage, Spark creatures 25% less.

title: Spark boss
short: Grove creatures deal it 50% more damage, Tide creatures 25% less.

title: Tide place
short: Tide creatures live here.
lines: Most creatures that live here are Tide.
Shards found here are Tide shards.
Gear found here is Tide gear: its lines lean Tide.

title: Ember place
short: Ember creatures live here.
lines: Most creatures that live here are Ember.
Shards found here are Ember shards.
Gear found here is Ember gear: its lines lean Ember.

title: Grove place
short: Grove creatures live here.
lines: Most creatures that live here are Grove.
Shards found here are Grove shards.
Gear found here is Grove gear: its lines lean Grove.

title: Spark place
short: Spark creatures live here.
lines: Most creatures that live here are Spark.
Shards found here are Spark shards.
Gear found here is Spark gear: its lines lean Spark.

title: Guard Charm
short: Only a Guard can wear it.
lines: Guard lines roll three times as often on it, and no other role's lines roll at all.

title: Support Charm
short: Only a Support can wear it.
lines: Support lines roll three times as often on it, and no other role's lines roll at all.

title: Setter Charm
short: Only a Setter can wear it.
lines: Setter lines roll three times as often on it, and no other role's lines roll at all.

title: Payoff Charm
short: Only a Payoff can wear it.
lines: Payoff lines roll three times as often on it, and no other role's lines roll at all.

title: Explorer gear
short: Made for trips, not fights.
lines: Trip and Workshop lines roll three times as often on it, fight lines much less often.
It is found at the Old Crossroads. Crafting it takes no shard.

title: Workshop
short: Your creatures work on jobs here, even while you are away.
lines: You can run 2 jobs at once, and each job needs a creature.
A creature on a job cannot go on an expedition, and the other way round.
It still fights in raids.

title: Blueprint
short: Teaches you to craft one kind of item. Learned once.
lines: Blueprints come from expeditions (more often on long ones), the welcome kit and sometimes a won finale.
A blueprint you know becomes a well-thumbed mark (up to 10). At 10 marks it turns into 5 scrap.

title: Common gear
short: A base stat or line and 1 rolled line.
lines: Easy to find and craft.

title: Rare gear
short: A base stat or line and 2 rolled lines.
lines: Can roll All damage taken, Lucky find and Adaptation pierce.

title: Epic gear
short: A base stat or line and 3 rolled lines.
lines: Can also roll Lingering and Unbothered at item level 15 or more.
Dismantling Epic gear can give glimmer.

title: Festival gear
short: Special, not stronger. A look and a line of its own.
lines: Won by clearing a Festival finale. It cannot be crafted.
Its item level and rarity follow the same odds as any finale piece.
It has one fixed Festival line and rolls from a short list of lines.

title: Item stat
short: An item's own Attack and HP (some add crit). It is added to the creature.
lines: It grows with the item level, and better bases carry more.
The lines marked (this item) change these numbers: first the flat ones, then the percent ones.
Charms have no stats: they carry a fixed line instead.

title: (this item)
short: A line that only changes this item's own stat.
lines: +60% Attack (this item) makes this Hat's own Attack bigger. It does not change the creature's Attack.
Every other line acts on the creature or on the fight.

title: Scrap
short: Generic parts. They pay for crafting.
lines: Found by dismantling gear, on expeditions, in cleared raid phases and in the daily dungeon.

title: Tide Shard
short: A shard of Tide. It pays for Tide crafts.
lines: Found on expeditions with a Tide explorer, from Tide room bosses and by dismantling Tide gear.

title: Ember Shard
short: A shard of Ember. It pays for Ember crafts.
lines: Found on expeditions with an Ember explorer, from Ember room bosses and by dismantling Ember gear.

title: Grove Shard
short: A shard of Grove. It pays for Grove crafts.
lines: Found on expeditions with a Grove explorer, from Grove room bosses and by dismantling Grove gear.

title: Spark Shard
short: A shard of Spark. It pays for Spark crafts.
lines: Found on expeditions with a Spark explorer, from Spark room bosses and by dismantling Spark gear.

title: Glimmer
short: A rare part. Epic gear and dungeon landmarks give it.
lines: Found by dismantling Epic gear, at dungeon landmarks, and rarely on expeditions (more often on long ones).

title: Craft
short: Makes a new item from a blueprint you know.
lines: Takes 3 hours and makes a Common. The item level is twice the creature's Crafting level.
The parts are paid when the job starts. The item is rolled when you claim it.
Reach for a Rare or an Epic costs more and takes longer. The Workshop shows the exact odds.

title: Reach
short: Pay Essence for a chance at a Rare or an Epic.
lines: Reach for Rare needs Crafting level 3 (25 Essence, 6 hours).
Reach for Epic needs level 6 (70 Essence, 1 glimmer, 10 hours).
One more chance to be a rarity higher: 1% for each Crafting level above 1 and for each well-thumbed mark.
You see the exact odds first, and there are no rerolls.

title: Well-thumbed
short: A blueprint you keep finding crafts better items.
lines: Each repeat find of a blueprint you know adds a mark, up to 10. A dismantle that finds one adds a mark too.
Each mark adds 1% to the chance that a craft of that item comes out one rarity higher.

title: Dismantle
short: A creature takes items apart for parts, Essence and blueprints.
lines: Commons go in bundles of up to 5 and take 15 minutes. A Rare takes 1 hour, an Epic or a Festival piece 2 hours.
The refund is a range shown first, a fraction of the craft price, rolled when you claim. Same for every creature.
Each item can teach its blueprint (6% and 1% for each Crafting level of the worker), or add a mark if you know it.

title: Crafting skill
short: Grows slowly each time a creature finishes a job.
lines: Each level above 1 makes jobs 3% shorter and adds 1% chance of a better craft.
It levels slowly: about level 5 after a month of steady work.
It never changes how a creature fights.

title: Daily dungeon
short: One run a day with a team of three of your own.
lines: Pick three creatures and the order they stand in, in one row. Then enter: the whole run is played out at once.
Three rooms: two foes, then a room boss. HP carries over. Clear all three to go one depth deeper; a lost run keeps it.
Clear the first room and you bring home a supply, guaranteed. Deeper runs drop better ones.
One run per day. The day resets at 13:37 in the server's time zone. A lost first run can be retried once.

title: Your row
short: Three creatures in one row, left to right.
lines: You choose the order. Your creatures act left to right, then the foe acts. Every room, every time.
The foe's plain attack goes to the left creature first, then the next one standing.
A Guard takes the hits aimed at the creatures right beside it, so it likes the middle.
A zone attack hits the one creature at its place. Silence hits the left and the right end.

title: Dungeon depth
short: How deep you are. Foes get tougher with every depth.
lines: Clearing all rooms adds 1. Losing leaves it as it is.
Every 7th depth is a landmark.

title: Room modifiers
short: Each room has a twist, shown before you enter.
lines: The day's three modifiers are the same for everyone on the server.
Some boost one element or one role, some change the foe, and some change your crits.
They only last for their room. Pick your team around them.

title: Room boss
short: The foe of the last room. Tougher than the others.
lines: It has more HP and hits harder than the foes before it.
Each boss has its own trick, and some are the same ones raid bosses use.
Beating it clears the dungeon for the day.

title: Landmark
short: Every 7th depth. A full clear drops gear for sure.
lines: Landmark depths are 7, 14, 21 and so on.
Clear all rooms on one to get a gear drop for certain, with better odds of rare and epic gear.
It also pays extra Essence, scrap and a glimmer.

title: Daily streak
short: Days in a row with a dungeon run.
lines: Your streak grows by 1 each day you run the dungeon.
The 3rd and 7th day of every 7 pay a bonus.
Miss a day and the count starts again. Your depth stays.

title: Flooded
short: Tide creatures hit 20% harder.

title: Scorched
short: Ember creatures hit 20% harder.

title: Overgrown
short: Grove creatures hit 20% harder.

title: Stormy
short: Spark creatures hit 20% harder.

title: Dark
short: Your creatures crit 5 points more often.

title: Thorns
short: The foe turns the first reaction of each round back on your team.

title: Brittle
short: The foe has 20% less HP but hits 25% harder.

title: Echoing
short: Guards and supports hit 50% harder.

title: Explorer rank
short: Each creature gets better at exploring.
lines: A creature earns explorer XP from its own trips, and more from longer ones.
Each rank makes its trips a little shorter. Ranks open places, the 24 hour trip and better choices.
Your slots come from all your creatures' ranks added together.

title: Familiarity
short: A creature's feel for one place.
lines: 1 star: 4 finished trips there.
2 stars: it has caught every creature that lives there.
3 stars: it has found a shiny there.
Stars open the deeper area and give small bonuses at that place.

title: Deeper area
short: A hidden part of a place, with rarer finds.
lines: It opens with 1 star at the place, or when you carry a lantern.
Some creatures only live in the deeper area.
Once it is open, its rarer creatures can turn up in your catches.

title: Push on
short: A choice that can come up when a trip ends.
lines: A finished trip may offer a goal: stay out a little longer for a reward.
A safe goal always works. A risky goal can fail, and then the whole trip brings nothing home.
Each goal is marked Safe, Risky or Very risky. Ignore the choice to come home as usual.
Better supplies and higher ranks make a choice come up more often.

title: Supplies
short: Optional boosts for one trip.
lines: They cannot be bought. The daily dungeon drops them, trips can find them, and you can craft them in the Workshop.
A trip carries up to 2, never two of the same kind.
Trips without supplies are free.
The best tier of every kind always brings a choice at the end of the trip.

title: Journal
short: Pages of lore, found on trips.
lines: A trip may turn up a page you do not have yet.
Pages are grouped by place, and some complete a set.
Read closely: the pages hint at how things work.

title: Journal set
short: A few pages that belong together.
lines: Find every page of a set to complete it.
Completed sets count towards your milestones.

title: Weekly special
short: One place gets a twist each week.
lines: Trips that start there that week get the twist, such as more parts or an extra catch roll.
In Festival weeks the special is the Festival Grounds.

title: Expedition slots
short: How many creatures can be away at once.
lines: You start with 1 slot. The 2nd opens after a few trips.
More open as the ranks of all your creatures add up.
A creature is away or working in the Workshop, never both.

title: Milestones
short: Tiny permanent bonuses for things you have done.
lines: Trips, places, creatures found, journal pages and raid reactions all count.
Each milestone gives a very small bonus, like slightly better odds of rare catches.

title: Destination
short: A place to send a creature.
lines: Each place has its own element, its own creatures and a deeper area.
Some places need explorer rank, some only open at night or in Festival weeks.

title: Lure
short: Draws creatures, and new ones.
lines: Raises the chance that a trip brings a creature, and that it is a species you lack.
Made in the Workshop from Bait and a little scrap.
Comes in three tiers: Plain, Sweet and Golden.

title: Map scrap
short: One or more extra catches.
lines: Adds extra catch rolls to one trip, and always at least one.
Comes in three tiers: Map Scrap, Inked Map and Trail Atlas.

title: Lantern
short: Lights the way to the deeper area.
lines: Opens the deeper area, even without stars.
Handy at Moonlit Reef, where the rarest creatures wait.

title: Satchel
short: More parts, and more finds.
lines: Adds to the parts the trip brings home and helps it find a supply.
Comes in three tiers, from the Small Satchel to the Explorer's Pack.

title: Safe goal
short: Always works.
lines: Stay out longer for an extra reward.
The extra hours are shown before you choose.

title: Risky goal
short: Can fail the whole trip.
lines: It may fail. The card says how risky it is: Risky or Very risky.
If it fails, the whole trip brings nothing home.
Coming home instead is always safe.

title: Craft supplies
short: Makes supplies for expeditions.
lines: Takes 1 to 6 hours by tier. The creature needs Crafting level 1, 3 or 5.
Costs scrap, shards for some tiers and, for a lure, Bait. One supply per job.

title: Boon
short: A good turn of the weather, for the whole valley.
lines: Every day has one Boon. It lasts from the daily reset to the next one.
It touches that day's raid stage, every dungeon run, and trips and Workshop jobs you start that day.
Higher Boss Ranks make Boons stronger.

title: Omen
short: A bad turn of the weather, shown a day ahead.
lines: From Boss Rank 3 every day also has one Omen, never the same one two days running.
Festival weeks have Boons only. A wild Omen can come from Boss Rank 10, at most once a week.
Higher Boss Ranks make Omens stronger, faster than Boons.

title: Forecast
short: Today's and tomorrow's Boon and Omen.
lines: Tap the wall calendar in the living room to read it.
A well-planned raid can meet a bad Saturday. Plan the team, or the dungeon run, for the day.
